comments.body:
Host inspection: the volume being unmounted is only half of it. **The declaration marker that would make gate admission REFUSE does not exist either**, so the fail-loud protection is inert rather than merely unarmed.

**Measured on the host, 2026-09-05 ~11:55 UTC** (read-only metadata only — I cancelled an earlier `du` when it ran long, given this host's documented IOPS-saturation history):

    $ mountpoint /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch
    /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch is not a mountpoint

    $ ls -la /var/lib/rebar/.gate-scratch-required
    ls: cannot access '/var/lib/rebar/.gate-scratch-required': No such file or directory

    $ ls /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch/
    rebar-gate-snapshots
    reviewbot-vnaa57x_
    semgrep-mcp
    tmpgvy_yxuz
    tmpqk2k1l2n.json

    $ lsblk
    nvme1n1   50G  xfs   /var/gerrit
    nvme0n1p1 60G  xfs   /
    nvme2n1   50G              <- the gate-scratch volume: attached, NO fstype, unmounted

So the directory is a plain directory on ROOT, and it is in ACTIVE USE — gate snapshots, a live review-bot clone, semgrep-mcp, and loose temp files are all landing on the root filesystem right now, which is the exact condition ADR 0112 created this volume to end.

**Why the refusal never fires, which is the part worth fixing.** `user_data.sh` writes two markers, and only AFTER a successful mount:

    touch "$GATE_SCRATCH_MOUNT/../.gate-scratch-required"   # DECLARATION, on ROOT, survives unmount
    touch "$GATE_SCRATCH_MOUNT/.gate-scratch-mounted"       # PROOF, on the VOLUME, disappears with it

and its own comment states the contract: *"Declaration present + proof absent => gate admission refuses instead of quietly repopulating the store on root."*

Both markers are absent. So the state gate admission actually observes is "no declaration" — which it reads as *this host has no dedicated scratch volume*, and proceeds on root without complaint. The design distinguishes three states but only defends against one of them:

- declaration + proof -> mounted, proceed. Correct.
- declaration, no proof -> volume vanished, REFUSE. Correct, and the case the design was built for.
- **no declaration -> assume no volume exists, proceed on root.** This host. Silent.

**The structural problem: the declaration can only be written by the thing that also does the mount.** `user_data.sh` runs at instance LAUNCH. This volume was attached by Terraform to an already-running instance, so that block has never executed here, and it cannot execute without an instance replacement. A host that acquires the volume after launch is therefore guaranteed to sit in the third state — the volume exists in AWS, Terraform believes it is provisioned, the alarm exists, and nothing on the box knows it is supposed to be there.

That is why this has been silent all night rather than loud. It is not that the guard failed; it is that the guard's precondition is written by the same one-shot path that was skipped.

**Consequences for the remediation plan.** Mounting alone is not sufficient and doing it naively makes things worse in one specific way: the live contents listed above sit AT the mount point, so mounting over them SHADOWS them — they keep consuming root while becoming invisible to `du` and to every read-only probe. That is very likely a contributor to the unattributed ~21 GB recorded on `cyclopean-bloodshot-hoatzin` (du accounts 21.24 GB where df says 42.4 GB), whose leading hypothesis was exactly "files shadowed under mount points".

So the sequence has to be: quiesce the consumers, MOVE the existing contents off the path (not just mount over them), mount, write BOTH markers, then verify `mountpoint` succeeds and gate admission sees declaration+proof. Writing `.gate-scratch-required` at any earlier point would arm the refusal against a host that cannot yet satisfy it and would block every gate on the box.

Worth considering as a follow-up rather than here: the declaration ought to be derivable from something that survives a post-launch volume attach — the Terraform-known volume id, or a systemd unit that reconciles markers on boot — so that "the volume was added after launch" stops being a silent state.

comments.body:
## Re-verified on the live host 2026-09-05 ~22:24 UTC (read-only SSM) — and ONE FIGURE HAS MOVED MATERIALLY

Everything in this ticket's description still holds, with one exception that changes the urgency.

```
lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINT,SERIAL
  nvme1n1        50G xfs    /var/gerrit   vol06fa2e77a9dd97527
  nvme0n1        60G                      vol0270fcf13709cf472
  ├─nvme0n1p1    60G xfs    /
  └─nvme0n1p128  10M vfat   /boot/efi
  nvme2n1        50G   ---     ---        vol06780b8557d1416b7   <- still raw, still unmounted

blkid /dev/nvme2n1                       -> NO FILESYSTEM
/etc/fstab                               -> /, /boot/efi, /var/gerrit ONLY. No gate-scratch line.
mountpoint /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch   -> is not a mountpoint
.gate-scratch-required                   -> No such file or directory
.gate-scratch-mounted                    -> No such file or directory
```

Live contents, mtimes at the moment of inspection (22:21-22:24), i.e. **being written right now**:
`rebar-gate-snapshots` (203 entries), `reviewbot-r7x216ij`, `semgrep-mcp`, and five loose
`tmp*` files.

**THE CHANGE — root has gone from 57% to 81%.**

```
                 ticket (earlier)      now
  df -h /        34G / 60G  (57%)      49G / 60G  (81%)   12G free
  df -h /var/gerrit                    11G / 50G  (21%)
```

Root has gained roughly **15G in about eleven hours** while gate scratch runs on it. The ticket's
"stable, which is why this is not a p1" assessment was true when written and is weaker now: at this
rate the margin is days, not weeks, and a full root takes Gerrit down with it — the exact coupling
S1 removed on paper. I am not re-prioritising the ticket unilaterally, but an operator deciding
when to take the quiet window should weigh 12G free, not 26G.

## Two findings that change the remediation sequence

**1. A `du` over this directory does not complete in a usable time.** I started a read-only
`du -sh --one-file-system` on the scratch tree at 22:30 UTC; it had not returned after **25
minutes**, so I cancelled it rather than add load to a host with documented IOPS saturation. So I
did NOT re-measure the 9.3G figure, and I do not trust it as current given root grew 15G. The
practical consequence: **the remediation must not depend on `du`** — every space check should use
`df`, which is O(1). The runbook I am writing does exactly that.

**2. The review-bot container binds the PARENT, so a host mount will not reach it.**
`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:305` binds `/var/lib/rebar:/var/lib/rebar`, not the mount point
(deliberately — the comment there explains that binding only the mount point would make the
declaration marker invisible and the guard unable to fire). Docker bind mounts default to
`rprivate` propagation, so **a mount created on the host UNDERNEATH that existing bind does not
appear inside the already-running container.**

That means an operator who quiesces, mounts, writes the markers and then merely `docker compose
start review-bot` gets a split brain: the host shows a correctly mounted, empty volume and every
host-side check says "fixed", while the bot keeps writing to the OLD root directory through its
pre-existing bind. **`docker compose up -d --force-recreate review-bot` is mandatory, not tidiness.**
This is not stated anywhere in the ticket or in `review-bot-ops.md`, and it is the single most
likely way this remediation gets declared done while remaining in effect.

Nothing was mutated: read-only inspection only, and my one long-running probe was cancelled.

comments.body:
## Deliverables, and the boundary I did not cross

**Nothing on the host or in AWS was mutated.** No format, no mount, no fstab edit, no data move,
no `terraform apply`, no service restart. Terraform was read-only throughout (`-lock=false`, so
not even the S3 state lock was written). The one long-running probe I started was cancelled
rather than left to load an IOPS-starved host.

### Deliverable 1 — `infra/runbooks/gate-scratch-mount.md`

A turnkey procedure for a RUNNING host, grounded in what was measured over SSM rather than in
what `user_data.sh` does at launch. Eleven sections; every action carries its own verification
(with the expected output) and its own rollback, and the point of no return is named.

Three things in it are not in this ticket and are the reason a naive sequence fails:

1. **Move the contents aside; do not mount over them.** A rename on the same filesystem is
   atomic and instant, leaves the mount point empty so nothing is ever shadowed, and turns the
   rollback into a second rename. Mounting over live scratch instead hides those inodes while
   processes keep writing to them, so the space is never reclaimed and is invisible to `du` --
   very likely a contributor to the unattributed ~21 GB on `cyclopean-bloodshot-hoatzin`.
2. **The container recreate is mandatory.** `docker-compose.yml:305` binds `/var/lib/rebar`, the
   PARENT, and Docker binds default to `rprivate` propagation, so a host mount created under a
   running container does not appear inside it. An operator who mounts and merely restarts gets
   a split brain in which every host-side check reads healthy while the bot still writes to the
   old root directory. The plan-review gate independently found this too, which is some
   corroboration that it is real and not a private theory.
3. **Markers proof-first**, diverging deliberately from `user_data.sh:237-238`'s
   declaration-first order. That script runs pre-service at boot when no gate can be admitted,
   so its window is empty; on a live host, writing the declaration first refuses every gate on
   the box until the proof lands. `chmod 0700` precedes both (bug `ad8d` AC3).

It also never uses `du`, because a read-only `du -sh` over this tree did not return in 25
minutes and had to be cancelled -- so every space check is `df`, which is O(1). A consequence
worth stating: **the 9.3G figure was NOT re-measured and should not be trusted as current**,
given root grew ~15G in the same window.

### Deliverable 2 — `scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py` (AC5, the delivery gap)

Terraform holds one half of the answer -- which volumes are attached -- and the host holds the
other -- which mount points are backed by a real filesystem. Neither is wrong alone; nothing
joined them. This performs that join and fails loudly, naming the volume and pointing at the
runbook, so "delivered but not in effect" is an error at apply time rather than an alarm noticed
days later. Three outcomes, not two: `UNKNOWN` (the host did not report the device) stays
distinct from `NOT-IN-SERVICE` and also fails, because "I could not tell" must not read as "it
is fine" -- the same conflation shape as the bug itself.

Two alternatives were considered and REJECTED, with reasons recorded in the module docstring so
they are not re-litigated:

- **A post-boot auto-reconciler cannot cover this case.** Auto-mounting an already-formatted
  volume is safe; this volume was RAW, and auto-`mkfs` on a volume that merely looks blank is
  how a restored backup gets destroyed. The unsafe half is exactly the half that was needed.
- **Flipping `rebar.llm.gate_admission` to refuse on a missing declaration is a real design
  change**, not a bug fix: the marker pair is deliberately opt-in by provisioning so no laptop
  or CI runner changes behaviour on upgrade, and landing the flip while this volume is still
  unmounted would refuse every gate on the box. Filed as `reportable-commutual-rooster`
  (`1064-8c4a-f399-41de`), linked `discovered_from`, and sequenced explicitly AFTER the runbook
  is executed.

RED-first and perturbation-checked: the headline test reproduces the ACTUAL production state
from the measured serials and requires it to fail; treating an unmounted volume as in-service
turns that test red, and dropping the dashless-serial normalisation turns three red including
the passing case (without it every volume silently becomes `UNKNOWN` -- a guard that fails for
the wrong reason). 9 tests, offline, no AWS.

### What I did NOT establish

- Whether the current on-root scratch is still ~9.3G. The `du` did not complete.
- Anything about how the host behaves AFTER the mount: no step of the runbook has been executed,
  so its verifications are predictions grounded in measured state, not observations.
- Whether the review-bot has other writers of `/var/lib/rebar` beyond the compose service and
  host-side `rebar` gate runs. I confirmed the compose bind is the only one in
  `docker-compose.yml`; I did not enumerate host processes (`lsof` was not run).

comments.body:
## The host REBOOTED at ~23:52 UTC, and it changes three things — measured, read-only

Gerrit went unreachable (`curl` refused on :443, `git ls-remote` reset). SSM showed `up 0 min`.
It is back now. Three consequences, all verified rather than inferred:

### 1. The remediation is STILL required, and the reboot did not help

```
lsblk   nvme1n1  50G xfs  /var/gerrit  vol06fa2e77a9dd97527
        nvme2n1  50G  --      --       vol06780b8557d1416b7   <- still raw, still unmounted
/etc/fstab                -> still no gate-scratch line
.gate-scratch-required    -> still absent
.gate-scratch-mounted     -> still absent
mountpoint gate-scratch   -> is not a mountpoint
```

This is the expected behaviour and it is worth stating plainly, because "have you tried
rebooting it" is the obvious wrong idea here: **cloud-init runs user-data ONCE PER INSTANCE, not
once per boot.** A reboot does not re-run `user_data.sh`, so it cannot format or mount a volume
attached after first boot, and it did not. Only an instance REPLACEMENT would — at the cost of
replacing the production Gerrit host. This reboot is therefore a direct empirical confirmation of
the mechanism this ticket describes, rather than a coincidence.

### 2. Root fell from 81% to 76% — relief, not resolution

```
before reboot   49G of 60G (81%), 12G free
after  reboot   46G of 60G (76%), 15G free
```

~3G of transient files went with the restart (the per-review `reviewbot-*` clones are gone;
`rebar-gate-snapshots`, `semgrep-mcp` and the loose `tmp*` files survived). The trend that took
root from 57% to 81% in eleven hours is unchanged — this bought hours, not a fix.

### 3. DEVICE NAMES ARE NOT A SAFE IDENTIFIER, and I now have a direct observation

At `up 0 min`, `df -h` reported:

```
/dev/nvme2n1     50G   11G   40G  21% /var/gerrit
```

One minute later `lsblk` reported `nvme1n1 ... /var/gerrit` and `nvme2n1` as the unmounted
gate-scratch volume — the original mapping. So the two reads DISAGREED about which device node
backs `/var/gerrit`, a minute apart, on the same host. Most likely the first was taken while NVMe
enumeration was still settling.

**Why this matters more than a curiosity.** `/var/gerrit` is Gerrit's data volume, and it is
mounted by UUID, so it followed its filesystem correctly and nothing was harmed. But the
remediation for THIS ticket runs `mkfs.xfs` on the gate-scratch device. An operator who had
copied `/dev/nvme2n1` out of an earlier note and run `mkfs.xfs /dev/nvme2n1` during that window
would have **formatted Gerrit's data volume.**

`infra/runbooks/gate-scratch-mount.md` already refuses that, in two independent ways, and I am
recording this because the reboot turned a defensive precaution into a demonstrated one:

- §0 and §4 both re-confirm the target by **SERIAL** (`vol06780b8557d1416b7`), never by device
  name, and §5 writes fstab by **UUID** for the same reason.
- §4 will not format at all unless `blkid` reports NO filesystem — so even a mis-identified
  device that already carries xfs is refused rather than overwritten.

No action is required from this comment. Nothing was mutated; every command above was read-only.

comments.body:
## The gate-scratch volume is IN SERVICE — verified on the host and in CloudWatch

Independently verified at 2026-09-06 ~02:55 UTC, after the runbook was executed. This is the state
change this ticket exists to produce: gate scratch is no longer on the root filesystem.

### Host state

```
mountpoint -q /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch   ->  MOUNTED

NAME          FSTYPE SIZE MOUNTPOINT
nvme1n1       xfs     50G /var/gerrit
nvme0n1               60G
├─nvme0n1p1   xfs     60G /
└─nvme0n1p128 vfat    10M /boot/efi
nvme2n1       xfs     50G /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch     <- was RAW, no FSTYPE, unmounted

/etc/fstab:
UUID=7ea719fd-f65c-4e8f-992c-d74410b5ea4c /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch xfs defaults,nofail 0 2
```

Mounted **by UUID**, not by device name — which matters on Nitro, where NVMe device naming is not
stable across boots and a `/dev/nvme2n1` fstab entry would be a latent boot failure.

### Both markers present, on their intended (different) filesystems

```
-rw-r--r--. root root 0 Sep  6 02:45  /var/lib/rebar/.gate-scratch-required        <- on ROOT
-rw-r--r--. root root 0 Sep  6 02:45  /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch/.gate-scratch-mounted  <- on the VOLUME
```

That split is the whole point of the design: the declaration survives an unmount while the proof
disappears with the volume, so "declaration present + proof absent" is a state gate admission can
detect and refuse on, rather than silently repopulating the store on root.

### Space reclaimed — the disk-pressure win

```
df /                 60G   34G   27G   57%      <- was 42G used / 70%, and 49G / 81% at its worst
df gate-scratch      50G  2.7G   48G    6%
```

Root fell **70% -> 57%**, roughly 8 GB returned, with 2.7 GB of gate scratch now living on its own
50 GB volume at 6% utilisation. The root filesystem is no longer the thing a review burst fills.

### The consumer actually sees it

Verified from *inside* the review-bot container, not merely on the host:

```
docker exec compose-review-bot-1 df -h /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch
/dev/nvme2n1     50G  2.7G   48G   6% /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch
```

This is the check that distinguishes a real fix from a host-only mount the containers never see.

### CloudWatch agrees, and the alarms cleared to OK rather than going blind

```
gate_scratch_mounted            latest datapoint = 1.0   (was 0.0 on every sample)
rebar-gate-scratch-unmounted    OK   (state updated 19:46:55)
rebar-gate-scratch-disk-high    OK   (state updated 19:46:44)
```

I checked the state values explicitly rather than inferring from the alarms merely leaving the ALARM
list. **OK is not the same as INSUFFICIENT_DATA**, and given this host's live probe-truncation defect
(metrics near the tail of the probe publish nothing, so alarms can leave ALARM by going blind rather
than by recovering) that distinction had to be established, not assumed. Both are genuinely OK on
real datapoints.

### Not yet ticked

The `[non-codebase]` acceptance criteria require an indented `provenance:` continuation line naming
environment, principal, privilege posture and instrument before they can be marked complete — the
close gate enforces this, and rightly so. I am recording the evidence here first; the AC ticks plus
their provenance lines follow, and that edit will stale the plan-review attestation and require a
fresh review before the close.

## EXECUTED: gate-scratch volume is in service on i-00880b2c7f13527c5

Ran `infra/runbooks/gate-scratch-mount.md` §§2-10 end to end on 2026-09-06 (UTC), via AWS SSM
`send-command` (no SSH on this host). All acceptance conditions met and confirmed from CloudWatch.
**Not closing** — leaving that to the operator.

### §0 pre-change state (PROVEN, read-only, 01:42 UTC)

```
NAME          SERIAL               FSTYPE SIZE MOUNTPOINT
nvme0n1       vol0270fcf13709cf472         60G
├─nvme0n1p1                        xfs     60G /
└─nvme0n1p128                      vfat    10M /boot/efi
nvme1n1       vol06fa2e77a9dd97527 xfs     50G /var/gerrit
nvme2n1       vol06780b8557d1416b7         50G            <-- target: no FSTYPE, no MOUNTPOINT

/dev/nvme0n1p1   60G   42G   19G  70% /
blkid /dev/nvme2n1  -> NO FILESYSTEM
grep gate-scratch /etc/fstab -> no fstab line
mountpoint /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch -> is not a mountpoint
.gate-scratch-required / .gate-scratch-mounted -> both No such file or directory
```

Matches the runbook's expected table on every row except `df /`, which read **70% (42G)** rather
than the documented **81% (49G)**. Benign drift: `root_disk_used_percent` shows 82% at 18:12 PDT
falling to 69% by 18:22, i.e. the disk-pressure pruner reclaimed ~12% between the runbook being
written and this execution.

### Authorisation for the irreversible `mkfs.xfs` (PROVEN)

Device resolved **by serial, never by name**, immediately before the format, with two interlocks:

```
  candidate /dev/nvme0n1 serial=[vol0270fcf13709cf472]
  candidate /dev/nvme1n1 serial=[vol06fa2e77a9dd97527]
  candidate /dev/nvme2n1 serial=[vol06780b8557d1416b7]
resolved DEV=[/dev/nvme2n1] matches=1
root=/dev/nvme0n1p1 gerrit=/dev/nvme1n1 target=/dev/nvme2n1
interlock: target unmounted OK
interlock: blkid reports NO FILESYSTEM on /dev/nvme2n1 -- format authorised
```

The runbook's warning about NVMe enumeration is not theoretical and reproduced here: **after the
reboot below, `lsblk` listed `nvme1n1` FIRST**, ahead of `nvme0n1`. Ordering moved within this very
session; only the serial join was stable.

### §3-§6 (PROVEN)

```
mkfs.xfs /dev/nvme2n1 -> mkfs_rc=0
/dev/nvme2n1: UUID="7ea719fd-f65c-4e8f-992c-d74410b5ea4c" BLOCK_SIZE="512" TYPE="xfs"

UUID=7ea719fd-f65c-4e8f-992c-d74410b5ea4c /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch xfs defaults,nofail 0 2
mount_a_rc=0
MOUNTED
/dev/nvme2n1     50G  390M   50G   1% /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch
grep -c gate-scratch /etc/fstab -> 1
findmnt --verify -> Success, no errors or warnings detected
```

Markers written **proof-first**, per §6, and verified as the *property* rather than the filenames:

```
/var/lib/rebar/.gate-scratch-required             10303   (ROOT)
/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch/.gate-scratch-mounted 10302   (VOLUME)
PASS: markers on DIFFERENT filesystems (10303 vs 10302)
drwx------. root root /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch
```

Ordering rationale, restated because it is load-bearing: the DECLARATION on root is what makes gate
admission refuse when the proof is missing. Writing it first would open a window in which every gate
on the box refuses; writing the PROOF first has no bad window, because proof-without-declaration is
exactly the (silent) state the host was already in. `chmod 0700` precedes both so no marker is ever
written into a world-readable directory.

### §7 review-bot recreate — the split-brain check (PROVEN)

`docker compose up -d --force-recreate review-bot`, then **from inside the container**:

```
/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch 10302
/var/lib/rebar               10303        <-- DIFFER: container sees the VOLUME
ls -a /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch -> .gate-scratch-mounted
/dev/nvme2n1     50G  390M   50G   1% /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch
/dev/nvme0n1p1   60G   42G   19G  70% /var/lib/rebar
write test: /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch/.writetest 10302  WRITE_OK
```

Confirmed `docker-compose.yml:305` binds `/var/lib/rebar` (the PARENT) — so §7's mandatory recreate
is correct as written. `compose-review-bot-1` reached `healthy`, `/health` -> `{"status":"ok"}`,
and served a review (`in_flight:1`) shortly after.

### §8 reclaim (PROVEN)

```
before: /dev/nvme0n1p1  60G  42G  19G  70% /     (43958564 KB used)
RM_DONE rc=0 at Sun Sep  6 02:59:38 UTC 2026
after:  /dev/nvme0n1p1  60G  19G  42G  32% /     (19800344 KB used)
```

**~23 GiB reclaimed from root; 70% -> 32%.** Ran detached on the host (finite tree, polled to
completion) rather than in-line, so it could not block the SSM worker.

### §9 CloudWatch — confirmed with DATAPOINTS, not StateReason (PROVEN)

```
gate_scratch_mounted            19:45 1.0   19:50 1.0   19:55 1.0     (was 0.0 for days)
disk_used_percent  mount=/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch
                                19:45 1.0   19:50 6.0   19:55 5.0     (was NO DATAPOINTS)
root_disk_used_percent          19:45 70.0  19:50 56.0  19:55 45.0

rebar-gate-scratch-disk-high   OK   since 2026-09-05T19:46:44 PDT
rebar-gate-scratch-unmounted   OK   since 2026-09-05T19:46:55 PDT
```

The caveat about the observability probe truncating did **not** apply: `disk_used_percent` resumed
publishing normally, and `probe_ok=1` / `probe_truncated=0` throughout. No ambiguity to report.
Live gate traffic is now landing on the volume — `rebar-gate-snapshots` and `semgrep-mcp` have been
recreated there and it is at 2.1G/5%.

### §10 detector (PROVEN)

```
$ terraform show -json > tf.json
$ python scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py --plan-json tf.json --instance-id i-00880b2c7f13527c5
in-service      vol-06780b8557d1416b7  /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch  -- mounted
in-service      vol-06fa2e77a9dd97527  /var/gerrit  -- mounted
exit=0
```

(Before this procedure it would have named `vol06780b8557d1416b7` NOT-IN-SERVICE and exited 1.)

---

## INCIDENT DURING EXECUTION — I wedged the host, and it is my error

**What happened.** Reaching for §2's quiescence evidence, I ran
`lsof +D /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch`. That recursively walks the tree and builds an in-memory
table; the directory held 226 snapshot directories. Memory went
`43% -> 33% -> 23% -> 21% -> 4%` available (`mem_used_percent` 95%), the SSM agent stopped pinging
at 19:09:18 PDT, and every `rebar/host` metric ended at 19:08. SSM went `ConnectionLost`; run-command
invocations sat `Pending` indefinitely. It did not self-recover in ~30 minutes.

**This was avoidable and the runbook told me so.** §1 states a read-only `du -sh` over this same
directory had not finished after 25 minutes and that "this runbook therefore never depends on `du`".
`lsof +D` is the same class of operation — worse, because it also allocates. I ran it anyway.

**Recovery.** Diagnosed against `infra/runbooks/gerrit-host-wedged-ssm-lost.md`. Distinguished this
from that runbook's disk-full case: root was at 70% with 19G free and EC2 status checks were `ok`,
so the cause was memory, not disk, and growing the volume was not indicated. Took protective
snapshots (`snap-01e10c794b7abcf0e` gerrit data, `snap-0bae90f11fb67532b` root), then
`aws ec2 reboot-instances`. SSM returned `Online` 4m20s later; Gerrit HTTP 200; all containers up.
The procedure then continued from a re-verified §0 (all preconditions still held).

**Cost:** roughly 35 minutes of host downtime (02:09-02:44 UTC), which took Gerrit with it.
Nothing was lost — no destructive step had run at that point; the `mv`/`mkfs` came afterwards.

**Note on the Gerrit restart:** the standing instruction was not to restart Gerrit unless a runbook
required it. By the time of the reboot Gerrit was *already* down as part of the wedge, and
`gerrit-host-wedged-ssm-lost.md` prescribes a reboot for exactly this signature, so the reboot
restored service rather than interrupting it.

---

## RUNBOOK DRIFT FOUND (each is a real defect, filed here rather than worked around)

**D1 — §2 names the wrong compose directory.** The runbook says
`cd /var/gerrit/compose 2>/dev/null || cd "$(dirname "$(find / -name docker-compose.yml ...)")"`.
`/var/gerrit/compose` **does not exist**; `/var/gerrit` contains only `site/`. The real project dir
is **`/opt/rebar/infra/compose`** (from
`docker inspect compose-review-bot-1 --format '{{index .Config.Labels "com.docker.compose.project.working_dir"}}'`).
The `find /` fallback would also have walked the whole filesystem on an IOPS-starved box. This is the
same class as the `nginx-edge-render.md` defect (`git fetch` in `/opt/rebar`, which is an rsync copy
with no `.git`).

**D2 — §2's `fuser -vm` quiescence check cannot work, by construction.** `-m` takes a *mountpoint*.
Before the fix `/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch` is a plain directory on root, so `fuser -vm` resolves to
`/` and lists **every process on the box** including `systemd`, `kthreadd` and every kernel thread.
The documented expectation "no processes listed" is therefore unreachable in the pre-fix state the
step is written for. Chasing a usable substitute is what led me to `lsof +D` and the outage.
Suggested replacement — bounded, no tree walk, no allocation:

```sh
for p in /proc/[0-9]*; do case "$(readlink $p/cwd 2>/dev/null)" in *gate-scratch*) echo "$p";; esac; done
for f in /proc/[0-9]*/fd/*;  do case "$(readlink $f 2>/dev/null)"     in *gate-scratch*) echo "$f";; esac; done
```

Both returned 0 holders here, in about a second, and combined with a stopped review-bot and an
unchanged top-level mtime that is strictly better evidence than the `fuser` line asks for.

**D3 — no step warns against walking the tree, where it matters most.** §1's "never depends on `du`"
warning is a parenthetical about *duration*. It should be a prohibition attached to §2: do not `du`,
`lsof +D`, `find`, or otherwise recurse `/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch` — it will exhaust memory and
wedge the host. Demonstrated tonight.

**D4 — §2 does not mention `rebar-autodeploy.timer`, which fires every 2 minutes.** A
`docker compose stop review-bot` is exposed to a deploy tick landing mid-procedure. I stopped the
timer for the window as a precaution. Reading `autodeploy.sh` afterwards shows the review-bot
rebuild/restart is gated on a source change and the host was already at target SHA
(`12a10f3ab4ef`), so it would have been a no-op — the risk is real but narrow, and it is only
narrow *because* `main` happened not to advance. Worth one sentence in §2. (The timer is `enabled`,
so the reboot restored it automatically; verified `active` afterwards.)

**D5 — §7 recreates only review-bot; confirmed sufficient, worth stating.** I checked every
container for a `/var/lib/rebar` bind, since any other one would have the identical `rprivate`
split-brain problem. Only `compose-review-bot-1` binds it. §7 is complete as written — but the
check is cheap and the reasoning belongs in the runbook:
`docker inspect <c> --format '{{range .Mounts}}{{if eq .Destination "/var/lib/rebar"}}...'`.

---

## PROVEN vs INFERRED

**Proven:** every transcript above — format, UUID fstab line, mount, both markers on distinct
devices, in-container mount visibility and write test, 23 GiB reclaim, CloudWatch datapoints, both
alarms OK, detector exit 0.

**Inferred (not tested):** that the mount survives reboot. The fstab line is by UUID with `nofail`
and `findmnt --verify` passes, which is the mechanism — but I did not reboot again to demonstrate
it, having already spent one unplanned reboot tonight. Cheap to confirm at the next planned restart.

Residual items §11 lists (gate admission still treating "no declaration" as "no volume"; the
expected mount set written per-volume in three places) are untouched and still open.

## The finding

Epic 6202's story **S1 (`aa40-cbda`) is CLOSED, but its deliverable was not in effect.** The
gate-scratch volume existed, attached, raw and unmounted; gate scratch ran on the ROOT filesystem
-- precisely the silent fallback S1 exists to prevent.

```
pre-fix (SSM, read-only): nvme2n1 50G no FSTYPE/no MOUNTPOINT, serial vol06780b8557d1416b7
blkid -> no filesystem; no gate-scratch line in fstab; both markers ABSENT; df / -> 49G/60G (81%)
```

AWS confirmed the volume `in-use` at `/dev/sdg` with a matching NVMe serial, so the device was
unambiguous. It was simply never formatted or mounted: `user_data.sh` runs under cloud-init on
FIRST BOOT ONLY, and the volume was created by a later `terraform apply`. The script is correct;
it never ran. A gap in the delivery path, not a logic bug.

Both alarms were correctly in ALARM throughout, so this WAS detected. What was missing is that S1
closed on code correctness without any check that the volume entered service.

## Why remediation was not a simple mount

`user_data.sh:236-238` writes two markers to deliberately DIFFERENT filesystems:
`.gate-scratch-required` on ROOT (survives an unmount), `.gate-scratch-mounted` on the VOLUME.
Declaration present + proof absent makes gate admission REFUSE rather than repopulate on root;
here BOTH were absent, so admission read "no dedicated volume" and gates ran on root.
`/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch` held LIVE working directories, so mounting over them would HIDE them
while stranding the bytes on root. The ordered procedure is `infra/runbooks/gate-scratch-mount.md`.

AC1-AC4 and AC6 are HOST actions, tagged `[non-codebase]`, discharged by an operator running that
runbook. The code deliverable is the runbook plus AC5/AC7's delivery-gap assertion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] [non-codebase] The gate-scratch volume is formatted, in `/etc/fstab` by UUID, and mounted at
      `/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch`. Proven by `mountpoint -q` and `lsblk` showing the fstype.
      provenance: environment=EC2 i-00880b2c7f13527c5 via SSM; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — `mountpoint -q` true; `lsblk` shows nvme2n1 xfs 50G at /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch; fstab line `UUID=7ea719fd-f65c-4e8f-992c-d74410b5ea4c ... xfs defaults,nofail 0 2`; device resolved BY SERIAL (vol06780b8557d1416b7), which mattered — lsblk ordering changed across the reboot in-session.
- [x] [non-codebase] Both markers exist on their intended filesystems, created in the safe order, and
      `chmod 0700` is applied. Proven by `ls` plus confirming they are on different devices.
      provenance: environment=EC2 i-00880b2c7f13527c5 via SSM; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — both present, and verified as the PROPERTY not mere presence: `stat -c %d` gives 66307 for /var/lib/rebar/.gate-scratch-required (root) vs 66306 for gate-scratch/.gate-scratch-mounted (volume) — genuinely different devices. Written proof-first.
- [x] [non-codebase] `rebar/host:gate_scratch_mounted` publishes 1 and `disk_used_percent` resumes publishing;
      both alarms return to OK. Proven from CloudWatch, not from the host alone.
      provenance: environment=EC2 i-00880b2c7f13527c5 via SSM; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — CloudWatch datapoints, not StateReason: gate_scratch_mounted=1.0; disk_used_percent for the mount resumed after zero datapoints; both alarms read OK. State values checked explicitly to distinguish OK from INSUFFICIENT_DATA, since this host's probe-truncation defect can make an alarm leave ALARM by going blind.
- [x] [non-codebase] The stranded copy under root is reclaimed and `df /` reflects it.
      provenance: environment=EC2 i-00880b2c7f13527c5 via SSM; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — `df /` 42G/70% -> 19G/32%, ~23 GiB returned; gate-scratch itself 2.1G of 50G (5%).
- [x] AC5 (the only NON-`[non-codebase]` criterion). Concrete edit target:
      **`scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py`** (new) with its offline oracle
      `tests/unit/test_assert_volumes_in_service_dcc3.py` (new). It joins the two halves nobody
      had joined -- terraform's `aws_volume_attachment` set against the host's mount table --
      and fails, naming the volume, when one is attached but not in service. Three outcomes, not two:
      `UNKNOWN` (host did not report the device) stays distinct from `NOT-IN-SERVICE` and also
      fails. Flipping gate_admission to refuse on a missing declaration is filed separately as
      `reportable-commutual-rooster` (`1064-8c4a-f399-41de`).
- [x] `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` binds `/var/lib/rebar` -- the PARENT of the mount point
      -- and Docker bind mounts default to `rprivate` propagation, so a mount created on the host
      underneath a running container does NOT appear inside it. This is what makes recreating the
      review-bot mandatory rather than optional. Repository-verifiable, so deliberately UNTAGGED.
- [x] [non-codebase] The review-bot container is RECREATED after the host mount, and the mount is
      verified FROM INSIDE it. Without this the bot keeps writing to the shadowed pre-mount
      directory while every host-side check reads healthy.
      provenance: environment=EC2 i-00880b2c7f13527c5 via SSM; principal=RebarBotNava; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — recreated per runbook §7 and verified FROM INSIDE: `docker exec compose-review-bot-1 df -h` shows /dev/nvme2n1 on /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch, and a write test lands on device 10302 (volume) not 10303 (root).
- [x] AC7 -- the delivery gap is closed as a CLASS, and ONE mechanism is CHOSEN rather than
      left as an either/or. **Chosen: the apply-time signal, not a post-boot reconciler.**
      Positive rationale, not elimination: a reconciler could safely auto-MOUNT an already
      formatted volume, but this one was RAW, and auto-`mkfs` on a volume that merely looks
      blank is how a restored backup is destroyed -- so that branch cannot cover the case that
      actually occurred, and a half-covering automation is worse than an honest check.
      **Invocation point, stated:** `scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py` is a MANDATORY
      post-apply step, invoked from `infra/runbooks/gate-scratch-mount.md` §10 after this
      remediation and after ANY future `terraform apply` that adds or replaces a volume.
      Operation-linked deliberately, rather than bound to one CI provider, which is what
      `project.portability` requires.
      **Why it is not ALSO wired into `terraform-drift.yml`**, as a checkable fact rather than
      an omission: that workflow assumes the `rebar-terraform-plan` OIDC role, which is
      `ReadOnlyAccess` + `kms:Decrypt` (`infra/terraform/iam.tf:178-191`). `ssm:SendCommand` is
      a WRITE action absent from `ReadOnlyAccess`, so that role cannot run the host probe at
      all. Granting it is an IAM widening with its own blast radius and needs its own ticket.
      A fix that only mounts this one volume by hand would leave the next to be found the same
      way -- by an alarm, days later.

## Verification

AC5/AC7: `pytest tests/unit/test_assert_volumes_in_service_dcc3.py` and
`python scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py --instance-id i-00880b2c7f13527c5` (must exit 0,
both volumes `in-service`). `[non-codebase]` criteria: on the host by `mountpoint -q`, `lsblk`,
`findmnt --verify`, `stat -c %d` on both markers (must report DIFFERENT devices), `df -h /`, and
`docker exec compose-review-bot-1 df -h /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch`; from CloudWatch by
`get-metric-statistics` on `gate_scratch_mounted` (=1) and `disk_used_percent` (resumed), with
both alarms read as OK, not INSUFFICIENT_DATA.
